stem: Farhan's group must measure the length of the same school corridor so their readings can be compared. Someone suggests each student's own foot length. Someone suggests the metre. Someone names the centimetre as the SI unit of length.

parts.text: Which claim is correct about a suitable shared length unit?

options.text: The metre is suitable because everyone can use the same agreed standard unit.
Each student's own foot length is a standard length unit.
The SI unit of length is the centimetre (cm).
The centimetre is not a standard length unit at all.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: A shared measurement needs an agreed standard unit; the SI unit of length is the metre.

teacher.key_rationale: Shared length measurements need a standard unit. The metre is suitable and is the SI unit of length. Foot length varies by person; centimetre is a standard subunit but not the SI unit of length.
